boundary_evidence: NOT FROM tu_map. tools/tu_map.py reports the arm9 `main` module as UNDER-SEGMENTED: one unit covering the whole module text with dozens of class labels, so there is no tu_map boundary or `tubuild.py create` candidate id here; every line below is hand-derived and independently checkable.
contiguous linker run 0x02014aa8..0x020150e8: the eleven delinks entries tile the span exactly with no hole (config/arm9/delinks.txt, config/arm9/symbols.txt).

class-label homogeneity: every named symbol in the run is a member of dCc_c (the cylinder-collision root in include/dCc_c.h). The two `func_0201*` entries inside the run are the TU's file-static helpers -- Process() calls func_02014f44 on a flag-8 hit, and func_02014f44 forwards to func_02014f5c; both are called only from inside the run.

ROM evidence says one object: the emitted vtable lands at 0x0208e6ec (_ZTV5dCc_c) and its typeinfo 0x0208e660 is a root __class_type_info carrying the name _ZTS5dCc_c at 0x0208e658; the three derived typeinfos (_ZTI8dCcPos_c, _ZTI7dCcAc_c, _ZTI10dCcAcPos_c) all point back at it as their base.

neighbour below: _ZN10dCcAcPos_cC1Ev at 0x02014a84..0x02014aa8 (a derived class). Neighbour above: _ZN7Clipper13Func_020150E8ER7Vector35Fix12IiEPh at 0x020150e8 (a different class). The run is bracketed rather than cut out of a uniform stretch.

compiler_only_output.reason: Complete-object variant of the base-subobject ctor _ZN5dCc_cC2Ev (0x020150cc): mwcc emits both from one out-of-line ctor, the retail link kept only C2 (the base chain every derived ctor enters) and no configured symbol names this copy.

Process() builds a stack Vector3 (diff) so mwccarm re-emits Vector3's trivial vague-linkage D1 alongside the licensed text. The cartridge keeps one copy at arm9:0x020072c0, kind:function(arm,size=0x4), owned by an enrolled source; rombuild compares this object's body against those cartridge bytes and refuses anything but byte-identical vague-linkage output before discarding the duplicate.

notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main, so there was no candidate id to create from. The schema follows the arm9/dFader_c and arm9/dWipe_c entries, which took the same route.

func_02014f44 and func_02014f5c are this TU's helpers: Process() calls the forwarder func_02014f44 on flag-8 hits. They now parse as C++ and retain C linkage; the notifier uses dActor_c::FindWithID and the inherited actorID member. The earlier C-mode recipe is superseded.
dCc_c::Update keeps its link-in body deslopped to named members (next/prev/this stores); the same writes the shard's void* puns emitted, measured byte-identical.

Init is the native method _ZN5dCc_c4InitEiijj (formerly the C-linkage name _ZN5dCc_c4InitE5Fix12IiES1_jj). Fix12i is a scalar typedef, and the method emits the same 24 retail bytes; the symbol and its callers were renamed together (issue #3791). The previous 6az class-by-value explanation did not apply to this signature.

The destructor definition is the key function: mwcc emits D2/D0/D1 from the one `~dCc_c()` and the cartridge keeps all three, so the compilerOnlyOutput list carries only the homeless C1 ctor variant. D0 ends with the class-local operator delete, which is Memory::operator_delete2 (0x0203cbcc) -- the class deallocates off the actor heap.
